MEMORANDUM — structural core (D1–D3) for S = {sorted 1≤a≤b≤c≤d, a²+b²+c²+d²=4abcd}, mutation x↦4·(product of others)−x then re-sort; root (1,1,1,1); height h(v)=d (decision 4). All proved from definitions SC1–SC2; no external materials exist (SC6).

LEMMA V (Vieta conjugate). If (a,b,c,d)∈S then d′=4abc−d is an integer ≥1 and (a,b,c,d′), re-sorted, lies in S. Proof: d is a root of t²−4abc·t+(a²+b²+c²)=0; the other root d′ has d+d′=4abc∈ℤ and dd′=a²+b²+c²>0, so d′∈ℤ and d′≥1; the equation gives a²+b²+c²+d′²=4abc·d′. ∎

LEMMA L2 (top tie only at root). If c=d then v=(1,1,1,1). Proof: the equation gives a²+b²=(4ab−2)d². Since ab≥1, RHS≥2d²; since a,b≤d, LHS≤2d². Equality: 4ab−2=2 ⇒ ab=1 ⇒ a=b=1, and 2=2d² ⇒ d=1. (Same as the suggested route: d² | a²+b² forces a²+b²∈{d²,2d²}; the first gives 4ab=3, impossible; the second is above.) Hence at every non-root vertex c<d: the maximum coordinate is unique; also a=d⇒c=d⇒root. ∎

LEMMA L1 (descent). At every non-root v: 1≤d′<d. Proof: d′≥1 by Lemma V. Assume d′≥d. Then d²≤dd′=a²+b²+c²≤3c², so d≤c√3. Then 4abc²≤4abcd=a²+b²+c²+d²≤2(a²+b²+c²)≤6c², hence 4ab≤6, i.e. 2ab≤3, so ab=1 and a=b=1. Now d²≤a²+b²+c²=c²+2<(c+1)² (since 2<2c+1 for c≥1), so d≤c; with d≥c, d=c. The equation becomes 2+2c²=4c², so c=1 and v=(1,1,1,1) — contradiction. ∎ Note: no Pell/mod-3 step is needed; the previously suggested exclusion of m²=3c²−2 mod 3 is invalid as stated (m²≡1 mod 3 occurs, e.g. c=1), and this route avoids it entirely.

LEMMA L3 (mutating below the max grows, factor ≥3). At non-root v, mutate x∈{a,b,c}: x′=4(abcd/x)−x≥4d−d=3d>d, because the other three coordinates include d (product ≥d) and x≤d. After re-sorting the new maximum is x′ (other entries ≤d<x′). So every mutation not at d strictly increases height, by factor ≥3 (for x=c the factor is ≥4ab−1). ∎

COROLLARY (no height-preserving mutation; the d-mutation lowers height). At non-root v: mutating d yields re-sorted (a,b,c,d′) with max=max(c,d′)<d (d′<d by L1, c<d by L2); mutating a,b,c yields max≥3d>d by L3. Hence every mutation strictly changes height. At the root the unique mutated vertex is (1,1,1,3), height 3>1. ∎

THEOREM D2 (unique height-decreasing mutation). At every non-root v exactly one mutated vertex has height<h(v): the one from mutating the maximum coordinate d; all other coordinate-mutations raise height to ≥3d. Uniqueness is at the level of vertices of the quotient (sorted) graph: if a=b or b=c, some of the four coordinate-mutations coincide after sorting (mutating a vs b when a=b gives the same multiset), but all such coincidences lie among height-increasing mutations, so the height-decreasing vertex is unique; since c<d (L2) it also comes from a unique coordinate index. No mutation fixes height. ∎

THEOREM D1 (connectivity). Define parent(v), v≠root: mutate at d, re-sort. By the Corollary h(parent(v))=max(c,d′)<d=h(v); by Lemma V parent(v)∈S. Iterating, height is a strictly decreasing positive integer, reaching 1 within d−1 steps; height 1 forces (1,1,1,1) (since 1≤a≤b≤c≤d=1), and (1,1,1,1)∈S as 1+1+1+1=4=4·1·1·1·1. So every v∈S is joined to the root by a mutation path. ∎

THEOREM D3 (rooted tree). The mutation relation on S is symmetric — coordinate mutation x↦M−x is an involution — so the quotient graph on sorted vertices is undirected. It is connected (D1). It is acyclic: in any cycle take a vertex v of maximal height; its two distinct cycle-neighbors have height≤h(v), cannot exceed h(v) (maximality), and cannot equal it (Corollary), so both are height-decreasing mutations of v — contradicting D2. Connected and acyclic ⇒ tree, rooted at (1,1,1,1) with parent as in D1; a multiple parent (a second lower-height neighbor) would contradict D2 identically. ∎

LABELED OBSERVATIONS (hand-checkable spot checks, reproducible by direct substitution; not an enumeration): O1: (1,1,1,3): 1+1+1+9=12=4·3; d′=4−3=1, parent is root; all four root-mutations give 3, so the root has exactly one child. O2: (1,1,3,11): 1+1+9+121=132=4·33; d′=4·3−11=1, parent (1,1,1,3); mutating c=3 gives 41: (1,1,11,41), max 41≥3·11 (L3 confirmed). O3: (1,3,11,131): 1+9+121+17161=17292=4·4323, from (1,1,3,11) by mutating a 1 (4·1·3·11−1=131); d′=4·3·11−131=1, parent (1,1,3,11). Hence (1,1,3,11) has exactly two children (mutating a vs b coincide since a=b): branching exists and the equal-coordinate subtlety is realized already at depth 2.

STATUS: D1, D2, D3 PROVED, no counterexamples, no induction failure modes (L1 covers every non-root vertex; termination uses only that height is a positive integer). No growth law is assumed or implied; D4–D8 belong to the sibling threads.

MEMORANDUM (D4, D6, rq1). Cited as proved (answer:work:003-struct-core-v2): at every non-root vertex, mutation at the max d strictly lowers d; mutations at a,b,c raise the max to >= (4ab-1)d >= 3d; the quotient graph is a tree rooted at v_0=(1,1,1,1); every vertex has <= 3 children (fewer when coordinates coincide), the root has exactly 1.

T1 (depth upper). Each child edge multiplies the max by >= 3, so d >= 3^{depth(v)} and depth(v) <= log_3 d.

T2 (crude count). N(H) <= sum_{0<=k<=floor(log_3 H)} 3^k = (3^{floor(log_3 H)+1} - 1)/2 <= (3H-1)/2. N(H) = O(H), constant 3/2.

T3 (depth lower). Child max = 4*(product of other three) - x <= 4bcd <= 4d^3. Let L_k = max of log_2 d at depth k: L_{k+1} <= 3L_k + 2, L_0 = 0, so L_k + 1 <= 3(L_{k-1} + 1), giving L_k <= 3^k - 1. Hence depth(v) >= log_3(log_2 d + 1). Two-sided: log_3(log_2 d + 1) <= depth(v) <= log_3 d.

T4 (rq1 dichotomy; Outcome A holds). (i) The a=b=1 locus is a single chain. Equation: 2 + c^2 + d^2 = 4cd. The parent of (1,1,c,d) is the re-sorted (1,1,c,d'), d' = (c^2+2)/d < d, again with a=b=1; descending to the root and inverting gives the chain v_0=(1,1,1,1), v_1=(1,1,1,3), v_{j+1} = (1,1,d_j,4d_j - c_j) with c_{j+1}=d_j, i.e. d_{j+1} = 4d_j - d_{j-1}, ratio r_j = 4 - 1/r_{j-1} increasing from r_1 = 11/3 toward 2+sqrt(3). Chain vertices with d <= H: O(log H). For j >= 2 (c_j >= 3), v_j has exactly 2 children: v_{j+1} and u_j; every a=b=1 vertex lies on this chain.

(ii) ab is nondecreasing along child edges. Mutating x in {a,b,c}: x' > d is the new max, so the child's two smallest entries are the two smallest of {a,b,c,d}\{x}: mutate a gives bc >= ab; mutate b gives ac >= ab; mutate c leaves ab.

(iii) The unique off-chain child of v_j (j >= 2) is u_j = (1,c_j,d_j,4c_jd_j - 1), max m_j = 4c_jd_j - 1 >= 12d_j - 1 >= 11d_j; its ab = c_j >= 3, so by (ii) every vertex of subtree(u_j) has ab >= 3 and every edge below multiplies the max by >= 4ab - 1 >= 11. The subtrees subtree(u_j), j >= 2, are pairwise disjoint (tree, distinct parents), disjoint from the chain (there b >= 3), and every vertex lies on the chain or in exactly one of them (descend to the root; the path leaves the chain at most once, since ab >= 3 is irreversible by (ii)).

(iv) Subtree count. Vertices of subtree(u_j) with max <= H sit at depth <= log_{11}(H/m_j) below u_j, <= 3 children each, so size <= sum_k 3^k <= (3/2)*3^{log_{11}(H/m_j)} = (3/2)(H/m_j)^rho with rho = ln3/ln11 = 0.4582 < 1/2.

(v) Summation. m_j >= 11 d_j and d_j >= 11*(11/3)^{j-2} (induction: d_{j-1} <= (3/11)d_j, so d_{j+1} = 4d_j - d_{j-1} >= (41/11)d_j >= (11/3)d_j). Hence sum_{j>=2} m_j^{-rho} <= 121^{-rho} / (1 - (11/3)^{-rho}) = 0.248, convergent since (11/3)^rho = 1.814 > 1. Therefore N(H) <= C*H^rho + O(log H), rho = ln3/ln11 = 0.4582, C = (3/2)*sum_{j>=2} m_j^{-rho} <= 0.372, an effective constant. N(H) = O(H^{0.4582}), sublinear; rq1 resolved by Outcome A.

CORRECTION to skeleton (v): d_j >= 11(2+sqrt3)^{j-2} is false (r_j increases to 2+sqrt3 from below); the explicit base 11/3 is used instead, with all conclusions unchanged.

Depth extremes: the chain is the unique slowest branch (asymptotic factor 2+sqrt3), so chain depth = log_{2+sqrt3}(d) + O(1); T1's log_3 is approached only through the root's small factors, and T3's lower bound is approached along branches maximizing each factor (child max ~ 4d^3 requires a,b,c comparable to d).

LABELED OBSERVATION (hand-checkable substitution, not an enumeration): struct-core-v2 O1-O3 realize v_1, v_2, and u_2 = (1,3,11,131) with m_2 = 4*3*11 - 1 = 131 >= 11*11 and 1+9+121+17161 = 17292 = 4*4323 confirms u_2 in S; it has ab = 3, so its descendants grow by factor >= 11 as claimed.

STATUS: T1, T2, T3, T4 PROVED; rq1 closed by Outcome A with explicit exponent rho = ln3/ln11 and effective constant C <= 0.372; no conjecture remains open in this thread.

hits.text: D5: Prove the strongest rigorous lower bound for N(H). HARD CAP 600 words, terse lemma-proof. SKELETON: (L-A, chain) Define c_0=d_0? No: v_j=(1,1,c_j,d_j) with (c_1,d_1)=(1,3), c_{j+1}=d_j, d_{j+1}=4d_j-c_j. Prove by induction via the Vieta root-swap (state once: if (1,1,c,d) is a solution, mutating c gives solution (1,1,d,4d-c)) that every v_j is a solution, d_j strictly increasing, d_j = ((2+sqrt3)^j + (2-sqrt3)^j... derive the exact closed form: d_j solves x_{j+1}=4x_j-x_{j-1}? Verify: d_{j+1}=4d_j-c_j=4d_j-d_{j-1}, characteristic roots 2±sqrt3). Conclude N(H) >= log_{2+sqrt3}(H) - O(1): an explicit c*log H lower bound with c=1/ln(2+sqrt3). (L-B, binary subtree, the upgrade) At chain vertex v_j (j>=2), child u_j=(1,c_j,d_j,4c_jd_j-1) has max m_j<=4 d_j^2 and (prove) its two children-by-mutating-the-1-and-c_j are distinct; better: prove every off-chain vertex has at least 2 distinct children (mutations at a and at b; if a<b they differ since 4bcd-a vs 4acd-b: show inequality in one line; if a=b they coincide — handle). Then the binary tree rooted at u_j: at depth t the max is <= m_j^{3^t} * 4^{(3^t-1)/2} (from max' <= 4 max^3 induction) >= ... take logs: log max <= 3^t (log m_j + log 2). So depth-t binary subtree stays under H when 3^t (log m_j+log 2) <= log H, i.e. t >= log_3( log H / (log m_j + log 2) ). Total vertices from this subtree >= 2^t. Optimize over j (smallest m_j gives deepest t): with m_2 = 4*3*11-1=131: t = floor(log_3(log H / log 262...)) giving N(H) >= 2^{log_3(log H) - O(1)} = (log H)^{log 2/log 3 - o(1)}. Compute honestly and state the exact proved bound with explicit constants: N(H) >= max( log_{2+sqrt3} H - O(1), c' (log H)^{log_3 2} ) where log_3 2 approx 0.631, specifying for which H each dominates. If the binary-subtree distinctness step fails, prove it or drop to the chain bound and say exactly why. No tables, at most 2 one-line substitution checks.

D5: Prove the strongest rigorous lower bound for N(H) = #{sorted solutions (a,b,c,d) of a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2=4abcd with d <= H}. HARD CAP 500 words, symbol-dense lemma-proof style, no prose motivation, at most 2 one-line substitution checks. Take as proved (cite, do not reprove): the quotient mutation graph is a tree rooted at v0=(1,1,1,1); every non-root vertex's children are exactly the distinct sorted vertices obtained by mutating a, b, or c. SKELETON: (L-A, chain) v_j=(1,1,c_j,d_j), (c_1,d_1)=(1,3), c_{j+1}=d_j, d_{j+1}=4d_j-c_j. Prove by induction via the Vieta root-swap (state once: if (1,1,c,d) is a solution then (1,1,d,4d-c) is a solution) that all v_j are distinct solutions with d_j strictly increasing and d_{j+1}=4d_j-d_{j-1}, characteristic roots 2+-sqrt(3), so d_j = Theta((2+sqrt3)^j) and N(H) >= log_{2+sqrt3}(H) - O(1) with explicit constant. (L-B, branching lemma) Prove: every vertex at depth >= 2 has at least 2 DISTINCT children. Cases: if a<b<c, mutations at a,b,c give distinct new maxima since 4P/x - x is strictly decreasing in x; if exactly one tie among a,b,c, mutation at c versus at a differ since c>a (the unique vertex with a=b=c is v1=(1,1,1,3), which has exactly 1 child - verify). (L-C, counting) Full binary subtree below v2=(1,1,3,11): along any edge max' <= 4 max^3, so by induction log2(max) at depth t below v2 is <= 3^t (log2 11 + 1); the binary subtree contributes >= 2^t vertices whenever 3^t (log2 11 + 1) <= log2 H, i.e. t = floor(log3(log2 H/(log2 11 + 1))). Conclude N(H) >= c' (log H)^{log3 2}, log3 2 = 0.6309, with explicit c' and threshold H0. Final statement: N(H) >= max( log_{2+sqrt3} H - O(1), c' (log H)^0.6309 ), both constants explicit; note which dominates. If the branching lemma has a gap, isolate the exact failing case and prove the weaker bound it still yields. Anything stronger (e.g. (log H)^beta, beta > 0.631) must be labeled CONJECTURE with the precise obstruction.

From first principles, prove the strongest rigorous lower bound attainable for N(H). Construct explicit infinite families of solutions with controlled height growth and prove their members are distinct: at minimum a single chain (e.g., (1,1,1,3) -> (1,1,3,11) -> (1,1,11,41) -> ... generated by repeatedly mutating the second-largest coordinate) giving N(H) >= c log H with an explicit constant from the chain's growth rate (analyze the associated linear recurrence exactly); then attack a power lower bound N(H) >= c H^alpha by exhibiting a subtree in which every vertex has at least 2 (or more) provably distinct children whose maxima grow by a bounded factor per level, and determine the best provable alpha. If a power bound cannot be proved, identify the precise obstruction (e.g., inability to control the growth factor along branching edges, or collisions between children). All families must be proved to consist of solutions (direct substitution into a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2 = 4abcd) and proved distinct.

Is the exponent rho = ln3/ln11 = 0.4582 improvable toward the true growth rate of N(H)? Specifically: inside subtree(u_j), bound how often vertices have the full 3 distinct children versus equal-coordinate coincidences, and how the per-edge factor (>= 11, typically much larger) distributes; combine with the lower-bound thread to decide whether N(H) = Theta(H^alpha) for some alpha or whether the true growth is polylogarithmic-times-subpower.

Attack question:raised:07d805ce56d7:rq-sharp: is rho = ln3/ln11 = 0.4582 improvable toward the true growth rate of N(H)? HARD CAP 700 words, lemma-proof style. Take as proved (cite answer:work:003-struct-core-v2 and answer:work:004-upper-depth-v3, do not reprove): tree structure; children = mutations at a,b,c; child max >= (4ab-1)d; product ab nondecreasing along child edges; the a=b=1 locus is the single chain with ratio -> 2+sqrt3; N(H) <= C H^{ln3/ln11} + O(log H). ATTEMPT THIS ITERATED DICHOTOMY, proving each step that holds and labeling the rest CONJECTURE with the exact gap. (L1, level-p slow locus) For fixed a,b with p = ab, solutions (c,d), c<=d, of c^2+d^2 = 4p cd - (a^2+b^2) are generated by the Vieta involution (c,d) -> (d, 4p d - c) as one or more chains; each chain has consecutive ratio -> 2p + sqrt(4p^2-1) >= 4p-1, so contributes O(log H) vertices with d <= H. Prove the number of chains is finite by bounding each chain's minimal element (descend until d' >= d and bound that configuration explicitly); if finiteness resists, state it as the precise gap. (L2, product jump) At a vertex with ab = p: mutating c keeps product p (chain step, factor about 4p); mutating b gives new product a c >= c >= b >= sqrt(p) and in fact a c >= p c/b >= p when c >= b... establish the cleanest TRUE statement: any child strictly increasing the product has new product >= p^{3/2} (since the new product is ac or bc with c >= b >= sqrt(p)), hence per-edge factor >= 4 p^{3/2} - 1 below it. Verify the boundary cases a=b and b=c in one line each. (L3, iteration) Level 0: the ab=1 chain (O(log H) vertices); its product-raising children have p >= 3 (proved: u_j has ab = c_j >= 3). Level 1: vertices with ab=3, i.e. (a,b)=(1,3): equation c^2+d^2+10 = 12cd; find its minimal solution(s) and show the chains (u_2=(1,3,11,131) lies on one, ratio -> 6+sqrt35 = 11.92; substitution check 1+9+121+17161=17292=4*4323) contribute O(log H) vertices; their product-raising children have p >= min(1*c, 3*c) = c >= 11, so factor >= 43. Iterate: if level-k slow product p_k satisfies p_{k+1} >= p_k^{3/2}, then p_k >= 3^{(3/2)^{k-1}} (doubly exponential), each level contributes O(log H) chain vertices plus subtrees of size O(H^{ln3/ln(4p_k-1)}) whose exponents tend to 0. CONCLUDE the strongest statement actually proved: ideally N(H) = O_eps(H^eps) for every eps>0, stating exactly what the proof needs (finiteness of chain counts per level and uniformity of the level O(log H) counts); if full uniformity resists, prove the second iteration explicitly - N(H) = O(H^{ln3/ln43}) = O(H^0.2922), contingent on the ab=3 locus being a proved finite union of chains - and label the eps-statement CONJECTURE with the exact missing lemma. Phrase any lower-side bracket conditionally on the sibling lower-bound thread (N(H) >= c'(log H)^0.6309) since it is being proved in parallel. No tables; at most 2 one-line substitution checks.

From first principles, prove the strongest rigorous lower bound for N(H). Compact plan: (A) The chain: define (c_0,d_0) = (1,3) and d_{n+1} = 4 d_n - c_n, c_{n+1} = d_n; prove by induction that (1,1,c_n,d_n) satisfies the equation (verify n=0: 1+1+1+9=12=4*3, and the induction step via the Vieta quadratic: if (1,1,c,d) is a solution then mutating c gives (1,1,d,4d-c), a solution by the Vieta root property - prove this root-swap lemma once) and that d_n strictly increases; solve the recurrence exactly (characteristic roots 2 +/- sqrt(3); compute the closed form for d_n correctly) and conclude N(H) >= log_{2+sqrt(3)}(H) - O(1), an explicit c*log(H) lower bound. (B) Power/super-log bound attack: at (1,1,c,d) with c >= 3 the child obtained by mutating a (=1) is (1,c,d,4cd-1) while mutating c gives (1,1,d,4d-c); prove these two children are distinct and that 4cd-1 <= 4*max^2; then consider the subtree generated by repeatedly taking either child, bound the depth reachable within max <= H (growth per edge <= 4*max^2 gives log-log type depth), and compute honestly what lower bound this delivers (e.g. N(H) >= c'(log H)^beta for the largest provable beta, or only c log H). Prove whichever is rigorously attainable with explicit constants; for anything stronger, state the precise obstruction as a labeled conjecture. All family members must be proved solutions (the Vieta-root lemma suffices) and proved distinct. KEEP COMPACT (well under 1200 words), no tables beyond 3 one-line checks.

D4+D6+rq1: Prove the strongest rigorous upper bound for N(H) and the two-sided depth-vs-log-H relation for the rooted tree of sorted solutions of a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2=4abcd. REQUIRED SKELETON (terse lemma-proof, HARD CAP 700 words, no tables, no digressions): Restate in one line each, citing as proved: mutation at max d strictly lowers d; mutations at a,b,c raise max to >= (4ab-1)d >= 3d; quotient graph is a tree rooted at (1,1,1,1); every vertex has <= 3 children, root has 1. (T1, depth upper) d >= 3^depth so depth <= log_3 d. (T2, crude upper) N(H) <= sum_{k<=log_3 H} 3^k <= (3H-1)/2 = O(H), explicit constant. (T3, depth lower) child max <= 4 d^3, so inductively log2(max at depth k) <= 3^k - 1, giving depth >= log_3(log2 d + 1); state the two-sided relation log_3(log_2 d+1) <= depth <= log_3 d. (T4, rq1 dichotomy — the main sharpening) Prove: (i) a=b=1 forces the vertex onto the chain: (1,1,c,d) satisfies c^2+d^2+2=4cd, and by the same descent argument all its solutions form the single chain v_0=(1,1,1,1), v_1=(1,1,1,3), v_{j+1}=(1,1,d_j,4d_j-c_j); chain ratio tends to 2+sqrt(3), so #chain vertices with d<=H is <= log_{2+sqrt3}(H)+O(1) = O(log H). (ii) Along any child-path (height-increasing), the product ab of the two smallest coordinates is nondecreasing (mutating a,b,or c replaces one of them by a larger value; check the three cases in one line each). (iii) The unique off-chain child of chain vertex v_j (j>=2, i.e. c_j>=3) is u_j=(1,c_j,d_j,4c_jd_j-1) with max m_j=4c_jd_j-1 >= 3 d_j; it has ab=c_j>=3, so by (ii) every descendant edge multiplies the max by >= 4*3-1=11. (iv) Subtree of u_j down to max<=H has depth <= log_{11}(H/m_j) and <= 3 children per vertex, hence size <= (3/2)*(H/m_j)^rho with rho=log 3/log 11 (=ln3/ln11, approx 0.458 < 1/2). (v) Sum over j>=2: since d_j >= 11(2+sqrt3)^{j-2}, sum_j m_j^{-rho} converges to an explicit constant; conclude N(H) <= C*H^rho + O(log H) with rho=log3/log11, i.e. N(H)=O(H^rho) sublinear — state C explicitly if cheap, else as an effective constant. If any step resists, prove what holds and label the rest CONJECTURE with the exact gap. STRICT BREVITY: symbol-dense lemma-proof style; omit prose motivation entirely.

From first principles, prove the strongest rigorous upper bound for N(H) = #{sorted solutions with d <= H} and the two-sided depth-vs-log-H relation, ASSUMING the tree structure (prove the per-edge growth and branching lemmas directly so the thread is self-contained where cheap). Compact plan: (i) at a non-root vertex, mutating any of the three non-maximal coordinates x gives a child with new maximum 4*(product of three others) - x >= (4ab-1)d >= 3d; hence max(v) >= 3^{depth(v)} and depth(v) <= log_3(max(v)); the root has exactly one child (1,1,1,3) - verify. (ii) Each non-root vertex has at most 3 children and the root exactly 1, so N(H) <= sum_{k=0}^{floor(log_3 H)} 3^k = (3^{floor(log_3 H)+1}-1)/2 <= (3H-1)/2 = O(H) with explicit constant. (iii) Two-sided depth relation: upper depth bound log_3 H from (i); lower bound from the coarse child estimate d_child <= 4*d^3 (since a,b,c <= d), giving log max(v) <= 3^{depth(v)} * C for an explicit constant C, hence depth(v) >= log_3(log max(v)) - O(1) along every branch; identify along which branches each extreme is approached. (iv) Attempt to sharpen the O(H) constant or exponent rigorously (e.g., exploit that the (1,1,c,d)-chain is the unique slowest branch and off-chain children grow by factor >= 4ab-1 with ab >= 2, so most of the tree grows much faster; try to prove N(H) = O(H^alpha) for some alpha < 1); if a sharper bound cannot be fully proved, state exactly what is proved, and label any improvement as CONJECTURE with the precise gap. KEEP COMPACT (well under 1200 words): theorems with terse proofs, explicit constants, no tables.
